<h1>asocialmedia</h1>

The social network that knows you back. One place for your people, your interests, and the wonderfully weird parts of the internet.

<br>

<br>

the internet got a little too divided.

Somewhere along the way, being online became a full-time job in app-switching. Friends in one place. Artists in another. Communities scattered across five tabs. That one incredible post you saw at 2 a.m.? Gone forever, probably. We don't think the answer is another walled garden.

asocialmedia is an decentralized social network being built to bring the good parts together: people, posts, communities, conversations, and the wider open social web. A place to make something, find something, meet someone, or simply exist without being treated like a walking advertising identifier.

Make a post. Fall into a niche community. Discover a creator with 12 followers who makes the coolest stuff you've ever seen. Get a little too invested in an argument about which Linux distro is best. Normal internet activities. We want a social experience that feels like a place you want to visit, not a slot machine you can't put down.

<br>

<div align="center">
  <h2>different networks. one universe.</h2>
  <p>Good conversations shouldn't end at the border of an app.</p>
  <img src="https://cdn.asocialmedia.cc/protocol-asm.png" alt="asocialmedia connecting the wider open social web, including Bluesky and Mastodon" width="100%" />
</div>

<br>

Bluesky has its people. Mastodon has its people. The Fediverse has entire worlds of creators, communities, photos, videos, and beautifully specific opinions. And asocialmedia has a world of its own to build.

We're working toward bringing these worlds into one thoughtful discovery experience through AT Protocol and ActivityPub, with other open standards to explore down the road. Not by pretending everyone already has an asocialmedia account, but by respecting where content came from and who made it.

The idea is simple: discover across networks, create on asocialmedia, and eventually interact across compatible networks too. Your original posts and communities belong here; the wider social web makes the horizon a lot bigger.

<br>

**Still being built**: Cross-network ingestion and interoperability are part of the roadmap that every pictured network is already integrated or officially partnered with us. What appears in asocialmedia will depend on protocol support, permissions, moderation, and compatibility.

<br>

#### aura!? yes, aura.

Likes are nice. Karma is a number. Aura is our take on reputation across the things you do on asocialmedia.

A thoughtful post, a useful answer, a contribution that genuinely helps a community those should count for something. Aura is meant to recognize participation and credibility beyond who shouts the loudest or happens to go viral on a Tuesday.

Think XP for being a worthwhile human on the internet. Without having to defeat a final boss. (Unless the final boss is replying politely to a terrible take.) And no, having a giant number shouldn't give anyone a free pass to be awful.

_If an idea makes the internet less human, we're probably not interested. If it makes the internet feel a little smaller in the best possible way, we're listening._

<div align="center">
  <h2>some things are not up for debate.</h2>
  <strong>NO ADS. NO DATA SALES. NO WEIRD LITTLE TRICKS.</strong>
  <p><sub>Not now. Not hidden in the roadmap. Not after somebody in a suit discovers the word “monetization.”</sub></p>
</div>

NO ADS. EVER. No sponsored posts sneaking between your friends. No “just one tasteful banner.” No unskippable video asking if you've considered buying a mattress.

NO SELLING YOUR PERSONAL DATA. Your interests, messages, and identity aren't inventory. We're building a social network, not a suspiciously well-funded spreadsheet.

NO DARK PATTERNS. No guilt-trip notifications, fake urgency, misleading toggles, or hiding the logout button behind twelve menus and a small woodland riddle.

NO PAY-TO-WIN SOCIAL REACH. We won't sell a shortcut to the top of everyone's feed. Good work should have a shot without a credit card attached.

NO AI TRAINING ON PRIVATE CONTENT WITHOUT PERMISSION. Zeph is here to help, not quietly pack your private life into a training dataset. Personalization and memory should come with clear boundaries and meaningful controls.

NO HOSTAGE-TAKING. We believe people should have real ways to leave, export their data, and make choices about their digital lives. We're not building Hotel California with a notification bell.

Also: no pretending moderation doesn't matter. A welcoming internet needs spam controls, reporting tools, accountability, and actual people making difficult decisions when necessary. “Anything goes” sounds fun until the bots discover your comment section. These are the principles we intend to build and operate by, not a substitute for published privacy practices or a promise that every planned control already exists. come hang out

### AI? Yeah, we use that.

Some of our artwork, banners, icons, writing, and code are made with a little help from AI. We're not hiding it, and we're not ashamed of it.

We welcome AI-assisted contributions, human-made designs, and everything in between. Just one rule: **understand what you're submitting, test your code, and don't make maintainers debug something you blindly copy-pasted from an LLM.**

Designers and artists are especially welcome. AI helps us get things done, but there's always room for human creativity to make them better.

**[Read our AI & Contribution Policy →](./AI_POLICY.md)**

_AI is welcome. Slop is not._

Three years of building, a lot of late nights, and more infrastructure bills than we'd like to discuss at dinner. asocialmedia has been developed out of pocket, with support through Singularity Works. There are no ads paying the bills, because there are no ads. We'd rather keep it that way with people who believe this corner of the internet deserves to exist. If that sounds like something worth keeping around, sponsor asocialmedia.

Support goes toward infrastructure and time spent building the thing, not towards buying a yacht for Zeph. (He has a couch. He's fine.)
